proposal.title: Quazimgow: a scalable media relay
proposal.summary: Quazimgow builds a scalable media relay for schools and associations.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Self-hosted video calls fail once more than a few people join. Schools and associations are depending from video conferencing every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a scalable media relay called Quazimgow. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Video conferencing belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/quazimgow/quazimgow, which 375 public projects depend on. Our team is working on video conferencing for 5 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/quazimgow/quazimgow. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 40650.00 EUR for 58 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Self-hosted video calls fail once more than a few people join. Schools and associations are depending from video conferencing every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a scalable media relay called Quazimgow. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Video conferencing belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/quazimgow/quazimgow, which 375 public projects depend on. Our team is working on video conferencing for 5 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/quazimgow/quazimgow. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 40650.00 EUR for 58 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
